title: Lost in Simulation: LLM-Simulated Users are Unreliable Proxies for Human Users in Agentic Evaluations

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing agent success rates and simulation calibration errors (Expected Calibration Error) between participants speaking Standard American English (SAE) and African American Vernacular English (AAVE) during multi-turn task interactions.

Stratifying United States participants into three age groups (18-34, 35-54, 55+) to measure how agent performance and simulation validity vary across ages, and how age compounds with dialect-based performance disparities.

Evaluating agent performance and the validity of simulated users by comparing task outcomes across participants from four different countries with large English-speaking populations: the United States, India, Kenya, and Nigeria.
